_comment: NOT LIVE YET. The fleet as the locked combat model of 18 September wants it: twenty-four buildable hulls (four starting ships and eight research unlocks a side) plus the three legend hulls, with Size, the 0-30 armor scale, and guns as counts of individual cannon of three kinds. Every field is verified against the Fleet Roster sheet in Drive. It sits beside ships.json rather than replacing it because swapping the roster forces the combat engine to be swapped in the same move - the old damage formula is guns x swing against hull, which on these numbers takes about fifty shots to sink what used to take one. See PLAN.md.

classes.name: Wayfinder
classes.blurb: A long-legged exploration transport. Two light guns are barely a threat, which is the point: nothing in a fleet action wants to spend a broadside on her, and the four companies in her hold get where they are going.

classes.name: Interceptor I
classes.blurb: Cheap, quick to lay down and not meant to come home. Four light guns and ninety of hull: dangerous in numbers against anything lightly built, and kindling to a ship of the line.

classes.name: Morningstar
classes.blurb: The Crown's first heavy warship, and deliberately a bad bargain. Eight heavy guns and real armour, against slow going, poor repair and an upkeep that eats a small island's takings.

classes.name: Sovereign
classes.blurb: The ship of the line the Imperium opens with: nine hundred of hull, heavy guns, a siege battery and six companies aboard. Four light guns is not a screen, so she wants interceptors around her or the fast ones get in under her arc.

classes.name: Vanguard
classes.blurb: What the Morningstar should have been. Less armour and fewer heavy guns, but normal speed, a third of the upkeep and a shipwright's dream of a repair rate — the most fleet for the gold the Crown can buy.

classes.name: Resolute
classes.blurb: A fast general-purpose hull that does a little of everything: five light guns, one heavy, a company aboard and enough bombardment to matter at a small harbour. Six weeks on the stocks, and upkeep that reminds you why.

classes.name: Bulwark
classes.blurb: The Crown's first long guns, on a hull built to stand still and be shot at. Seven hundred of hull behind heavy armour — and not one light gun, so anything fast that gets close is somebody else's problem.

classes.name: Vanguard II
classes.blurb: The Vanguard grown up: more of everything that mattered and the best repair rate in the Imperium. Mends three per cent of herself a day, which over a long war is worth more than another gundeck.

classes.name: Interceptor II
classes.blurb: Ten light guns and five long ones on something that cannot be caught. She runs down anything trying to break off and cannot be run down herself — and a hundred and fifty of hull means she must not be made to stand and trade.

classes.name: Justiciar
classes.blurb: Every gun the Imperium knows how to make, on one hull, with nowhere to put a single company. Twenty-four cannon across all three kinds: she is for killing ships and she is not for anything else.

classes.name: Sovereign II
classes.blurb: A Sovereign that can keep up with the fleet. Fourteen heavy guns, twelve hundred of hull, nine companies and a siege train — and three light guns, so she still needs somebody watching the water around her.

classes.name: Majestic
classes.blurb: Thirty-six guns, armour nothing else in the world carries, sixteen hundred of hull and twelve companies. No single ship afloat beats her. She costs two and a half thousand, takes the better part of three years to build, and cannot get out of anyone's way.

classes.name: Swift
classes.blurb: Not a warship and never pretending. No guns at all, seventy of hull, and faster than anything that might want her — she is how the Confederacy finds out what is out there, and half a gold a day to keep.

classes.name: Brigantine
classes.blurb: A merchantman with two guns bolted on and her hold cleared for two companies. Fast, cheap, quick to build and honest about what she is: a commercial hull that never expected to be shot at.

classes.name: Chimera
classes.blurb: Built out of three other ships and whatever the yard had. Mismatched armour and salvaged guns make her slow and awkward and surprisingly hard to sink — three hundred and fifty of hull behind plate nobody can account for.

classes.name: Tidestalker
classes.blurb: Grown rather than built, by the reef peoples, and she closes her own wounds at four per cent a day. Five light guns and almost no armour: she will not win a stand-up fight, and she will still be on station next month when the thing that hurt her is not.

classes.name: Marauder
classes.blurb: Seven guns, two companies and a raiding mortar on a hull that costs a hundred and seventy-five gold. No armour and not much hull, but she goes where she likes and takes a landing party with her.

classes.name: Cutlass
classes.blurb: The Brethren's first ship built to fight rather than adapted to it. Two heavy guns and five light on a small compact hull — no companies, no siege battery, nothing but the action.

classes.name: Tempest
classes.blurb: The Confederacy's long guns arrive on something fast enough to use them. Four of them, real armour, three companies and a bombardment train, for two hundred and twenty gold and eight weeks — the best bargain in either navy.

classes.name: Reefwarden
classes.blurb: Grown to answer the Imperium's ships of the line. Seven heavy guns and heavy armour on a hull that mends itself, with four companies in her — no long guns, no siege battery, and a year and a half in the water before she floats.

classes.name: Ironback
classes.blurb: Eight long guns and the heaviest siege train in the Brethren, on seven hundred and fifty of armoured hull. She stands off a harbour and takes it apart. Put her in a fleet action and she has one heavy gun, no light guns, and nothing to do.

classes.name: Blackfin
classes.blurb: Twelve light guns — the heaviest battery of them in the world — on a fast hull with almost nothing over her timbers. She shreds anything small and unarmoured and she cannot scratch a first-rate.

classes.name: Urskin Whaler
classes.blurb: The largest hull anywhere: eighteen hundred, thirteen heavy guns and nine companies, out of the Urskin whaling yards. No light guns at all, so she is blind to anything quick, and she is slow, and she still decides invasions.

classes.name: Coral-Class Dreadnaught
classes.blurb: Twenty-four guns across all three kinds, armour a point short of the Majestic's, and she grows four per cent of herself back every day. Two thousand two hundred gold and nine hundred days of growing — the Brethren commit to her years before they need her.

classes.name: Open Deck
classes.blurb: Commodore-Elect Adaira Hale's ship: Corwin Calloway's old coral-grown three-decker, named for what he meant her to be, since any deck of his stood open to anyone the Crown wanted. The Moot was called on her quarterdeck and has been the Moot ever since. Where Hale is, the Moot sits — the hull was never the point, and nobody has seen it in years.

classes.name: Swallowtail
classes.blurb: Captain Silas Reyne's coral-grown sloop, which should not be as fast as she is and has never once been caught. Reyne is not off her for a night in his life, so far as anyone tells it, and that is the whole of why he turns up where he does when he does — a week's sail in half a week, every time, and no explanation offered.

classes.name: Adamant
classes.blurb: The Crown dreadnought Admiral Dorian Jessup took with him when he left the Imperium's service, and fought the Crown's own line with for nine years. What he learned aboard her he teaches to whatever squadron is lying in the harbor he is posted to, which is worth more to the Confederacy now than the ship ever was.
